examples.en: The booking system is a house of cards.
examples.zh: 這個預約系統十分脆弱。

examples.en: The project was a house of cards from the beginning.
examples.zh: 這個項目從一開始便十分脆弱。

meaning.en: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.
meaning.zh: 一個表面上看似完整或成功，實際上卻十分脆弱的計劃、系統、組織、論點或情況；其中一個部分一旦出錯，整體便可能迅速瓦解。
naturalZh: 一個表面上看似完整或成功，實際上卻十分脆弱的計劃、系統、組織、論點或情況
其中一個部分一旦出錯，整體便可能迅速瓦解。

register.summaryEn: For teaching purposes, a house of cards is best treated as a neutral-to-informal figurative expression with a strongly critical or warning tone.
register.summaryZh: 在教學上，a house of cards 可視為中性至非正式的比喻表達，通常帶有明顯的批評或警告語氣。
contextsEn: explanations of weak arguments or systems
contextsZh: 分析基礎薄弱的論點或系統。
register.formalEn: For teaching purposes, a house of cards is best treated as a neutral-to-informal figurative expression with a strongly critical or warning tone.
register.formalZh: 最後的名詞 cards 必須使用複數形式。

fixedVariable.fixedEn: Keep the fixed words and word order shown in the source expression.
fixedVariable.fixedZh: 保留原檔目標表達中的固定字詞及字序。
fixedVariable.variableEn: Change only the verb form, possessive, tense or surrounding grammar permitted by the source patterns.
fixedVariable.variableZh: 只按照原檔句式改變動詞形式、所有格、時態或前後文法。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式一：基本連繫動詞句式
specificForms.formula: Subject + be + a house of cards.
specificForms.descriptionEn: This is the most direct and common teaching frame.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 這是最直接和最基本的教學句式。

examples.en: The booking system is a house of cards.
examples.zh: 這個預約系統十分脆弱。

specificForms.formula: Subject + was / were + a house of cards.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Source grammar frame: Subject + was / were + a house of cards.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 原檔列出的句法框架：Subject + was / were + a house of cards。

examples.en: The project was a house of cards from the beginning.
examples.zh: 這個項目從一開始便十分脆弱。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式三：become 或 turn into
specificForms.formula: Subject + become / became / has become + a house of cards.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Source grammar frame: Subject + become / became / has become + a house of cards.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 原檔列出的句法框架：Subject + become / became / has become + a house of cards。

examples.en: The service has become a house of cards.
examples.zh: 這項服務已變得十分脆弱。

examples.en: The programme might turn into a house of cards.
examples.zh: 這個計劃可能會變成一個極不穩固的體系。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式四：look 或 seem like
specificForms.formula: Subject + look(s) / seem(s) + like + a house of cards.
specificForms.descriptionEn: The use of like creates a comparison with a physical structure made from cards.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 使用 like 會把某個系統與用紙牌搭成的脆弱結構作比較。

examples.en: The system is starting to look like a house of cards.
examples.zh: 這個系統開始顯得十分脆弱。

specificForms.formula: Subject + may / might / could / will / would + be + a house of cards.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Source grammar frame: Subject + may / might / could / will / would + be + a house of cards.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 原檔列出的句法框架：Subject + may / might / could / will / would + be + a house of cards。

examples.en: The plan may be a house of cards.
examples.zh: 這個計劃可能十分脆弱。

examples.en: Without emergency savings, the plan would be a house of cards.
examples.zh: 假如沒有應急儲蓄，這個計劃便會十分脆弱。

specificForms.titleEn: Collapse Like a House of Cards
specificForms.titleZh: 句式六：像紙牌屋一樣崩潰
specificForms.formula: Subject + collapse / fall apart + like + a house of cards.
specificForms.descriptionEn: This frame focuses on the actual or possible collapse rather than only describing the weak condition.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 這個句式把重點放在實際或可能發生的崩潰，而不只是描述系統本身脆弱。

examples.en: The whole system collapsed like a house of cards.
examples.zh: 整個系統像紙牌屋一樣迅速崩潰。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式七：建立一個脆弱體系
specificForms.formula: Subject + build / create + a house of cards + by + verb-ing.
specificForms.descriptionEn: This frame describes the actions that created the unstable situation.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 這個句式說明甚麼行動造成了不穩固的情況。

examples.en: The owner built a house of cards by borrowing more and more money.
examples.zh: 店主不斷借入更多款項，建立了一個極不穩固的財務體系。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式八：對比或揭示真相
specificForms.descriptionEn: Source grammar frame: a house of cards.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 原檔列出的句法框架：a house of cards。

examples.en: Although X appears strong, it is a house of cards.
examples.zh: 雖然某事看似穩固，實際上卻十分脆弱。

examples.en: What appears to be X may actually be a house of cards.
examples.zh: 表面看似某種穩固安排的事物，實際上可能十分脆弱。

benefits.titleZh: 清楚指出隱藏的脆弱之處
benefits.en: The expression contrasts appearance with reality.
benefits.zh: 這個表達可以對比表面和實際情況。 這個計劃看似完整，實際上卻十分脆弱。

examples.en: The plan is a house of cards.
examples.zh: 這個計劃看似完整，實際上卻十分脆弱。

benefits.titleEn: It Connects One Weak Part with Wider Failure
benefits.titleZh: 把一個薄弱環節與整體失敗連繫起來
benefits.en: The idiom helps speakers explain that one problem may affect an entire connected system.
benefits.zh: 這個慣用語有助說明一個問題可能影響整個互相連繫的系統。 這份時間表十分脆弱，因為每項活動都依賴第一項活動準時開始。

examples.en: The schedule is a house of cards because every activity depends on the first one starting on time.
examples.zh: 這份時間表十分脆弱，因為每項活動都依賴第一項活動準時開始。

benefits.en: The expression can warn listeners that apparent success should not make them feel too confident.
benefits.zh: 這個表達可以提醒聽者，不要因表面上的成功而過分放心。 假如沒有後備安排，整項服務可能會像紙牌屋一樣崩潰。

examples.en: Without a backup, the whole service could collapse like a house of cards.
examples.zh: 假如沒有後備安排，整項服務可能會像紙牌屋一樣崩潰。

benefits.titleEn: It Evaluates Plans and Arguments Efficiently
benefits.en: Instead of listing every weakness again, a speaker can give one clear overall judgement.
benefits.zh: 說話者不需要重新列出所有弱點，也可以作出一個清晰的整體評價。

benefits.titleEn: It Works with Present, Past and Future Situations
benefits.titleZh: 可以描述現在、過去及未來情況
benefits.en: It Works with Present, Past and Future Situations
benefits.zh: 可以描述現在、過去及未來情況

benefits.titleEn: It Is Vivid but Should Not Be Overused
benefits.titleZh: 形象鮮明，但不應過度使用
benefits.en: The idiom is not automatically better than weak, unstable or badly planned. Use it when the image of connected parts and possible total collapse genuinely fits the situation.
benefits.zh: 這個慣用語並非必定比 weak、unstable 或 badly planned 更好。 只有當「多個部分互相支撐，並可能全面瓦解」的畫面確實符合情況時，才應使用。

origin.statusEn: Well Documented; Exact First Spoken Use Unknown
origin.statusZh: 有較充分記錄；確切首次口語用法不明

history.en: Merriam-Webster dates the first known figurative use to 1645. The Online Etymology Dictionary similarly records the figurative sense in the 1640s and connects it with the familiar activity of building card structures. These dates refer to surviving written records, not necessarily the first time anybody spoke the expression.
history.zh: 根據 Merriam-Webster，現時已知最早的比喻用法可追溯至1645年。 《Online Etymology Dictionary》同樣把比喻意思記錄於十七世紀四十年代，並把它與搭建紙牌結構的活動連繫起來。 這些日期代表目前保存下來的文字記錄，不一定是人們首次在口語中使用這個表達的時間。

history.en: The physical structure provided a natural image for any plan or system whose parts appear organised but do not have strong support. Just as one card can affect the whole structure, one failed part can destroy the wider arrangement.
history.zh: 紙牌結構自然成為一個比喻，用來形容部分看似排列完整、實際上卻缺乏穩固支撐的計劃或系統。 正如一張紙牌可能影響整個結構，一個部分失效也可能破壞整體安排。

origin.memoryEn: One weak card can bring down the whole house; one weak part can bring down the whole system.
origin.memoryZh: 一張不穩的紙牌可以令整座紙牌屋倒下；一個薄弱環節也可以令整個系統瓦解。

rules.titleZh: 規則一：保留不定冠詞 a
rules.en: The expression normally uses a when classifying a particular plan or system as one example of this type of weak structure.
rules.zh: 當我們把某個計劃或系統歸類為這種脆弱結構時，通常必須使用 a。

rules.titleZh: 規則二：cards 必須使用複數
rules.en: A physical card structure is made from several playing cards, so the fixed expression retains the plural noun.
rules.zh: 實際的紙牌屋由多張紙牌組成，因此固定表達保留複數名詞 cards。

rules.titleEn: Use It for a Whole Plan, System or Situation
rules.titleZh: 規則三：用來描述整體計劃、系統或情況
rules.en: a business; an organisation; an argument; a budget; a schedule; a project; an arrangement; a claim. The expression normally evaluates an organised whole, not one small object or isolated action.
rules.zh: 合適的主語包括計劃、系統、生意、組織、論點、預算、時間表、項目、安排或說法。 這個表達通常用來評價一個有多個部分的整體，而不是一件小物件或一次獨立行動。

rules.titleZh: 規則四：脆弱程度必須相當嚴重
rules.en: A small imperfection does not normally justify the strength of the idiom.
rules.zh: 一次延遲付款便可能令整個項目停頓。 這個項目極不穩固。 項目有一個串字錯誤。 一個小錯誤通常不足以支持這個慣用語所表達的強烈程度。

examples.en: The project is a house of cards.
examples.zh: 一次延遲付款便可能令整個項目停頓。這個項目極不穩固。

rules.titleEn: The Parts Often Depend on One Another
rules.titleZh: 規則五：不同部分通常互相依賴
rules.en: 1. several parts depend on one weak part; 2. one failure would affect everything else; 3. there is no backup plan; 4. success depends on many uncertain conditions; 5. the system only appears stable.
rules.zh: 在以下情況中，這個表達尤其自然：

rules.titleZh: 規則六：保留確定程度及時間
rules.en: The incorrect answer changes a present possibility into a completed past fact.
rules.zh: 錯誤答案把現在的可能性改成了已確定的過去事實。

rules.titleEn: “Be a House of Cards” and Collapse Like a
rules.en: Focus: The system is weak now. Focus: The system failed quickly and completely.
rules.zh: be a house of cards 和 collapse like a house of cards 的重點不同重點：系統目前十分脆弱。 重點：系統迅速而全面地崩潰。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Same Meaning
rules.titleZh: 規則八：不要重複相同意思
rules.en: The final words merely explain the idiom again. The reason is preserved, but the meaning of weakness is expressed only once.
rules.zh: 後半句只是再次解釋慣用語的意思。 這個計劃十分脆弱，因為它依賴一個未經測試的想法。 原因得以保留，但「十分脆弱」這個意思只表達一次。

examples.en: The plan is a house of cards because it depends on one untested idea.
examples.zh: 這個計劃十分脆弱，因為它依賴一個未經測試的想法。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse the Literal and Figurative
rules.titleZh: 規則九：不要混淆字面和比喻意思
rules.en: Every answer in this exercise must use the figurative meaning.
rules.zh: 孩子在桌上用紙牌搭了一座小屋。 這盤生意十分脆弱，因為它只依賴一名顧客。 本練習中的所有答案都必須使用比喻意思。

examples.en: The children built a house of cards on the table.
examples.zh: 孩子在桌上用紙牌搭了一座小屋。

examples.en: The business was a house of cards because it depended on one customer.
examples.zh: 這盤生意十分脆弱，因為它只依賴一名顧客。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use It Merely for Something Complicated
rules.titleZh: 規則十：不能只因事情複雜便使用
rules.en: A complicated plan may still be strong and carefully prepared. The idiom is licensed only when the source shows serious instability or a real danger of wider failure.
rules.zh: 一個複雜的計劃仍然可能十分穩固和周全。 只有當原句顯示嚴重不穩定或整體失敗的真正風險時，才適合使用這個慣用語。

instructions.en: Rewrite or respond to each item using a house of cards.
instructions.zh: 使用 a house of cards 改寫句子或完成回應。

questions.prompt: The booking system depends on one old computer. If that computer stops working, the whole system stops.
questions.promptZh: 預約系統完全依賴一部舊電腦。假如那部電腦停止運作，整個系統便會停下來。
questions.answer: The booking system is a house of cards because it depends on one old computer.
questions.answerZh: 這個預約系統十分脆弱，因為它完全依賴一部舊電腦。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: The school trip plan will fail if the only bus is unavailable.
questions.promptZh: 假如唯一一輛旅遊巴無法使用，學校旅行計劃便會失敗。
questions.answer: The school trip plan is a house of cards because it depends on one bus.
questions.answerZh: 學校旅行計劃十分脆弱，因為它依賴唯一一輛旅遊巴。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: The business depends on one customer for almost all its income.
questions.promptZh: 這盤生意幾乎所有收入都來自同一名顧客。
questions.answer: The business is a house of cards because it depends on one customer.
questions.answerZh: 這盤生意的基礎十分脆弱，因為它依賴同一名顧客。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: The budget works only if every ticket is sold.
questions.promptZh: 這份預算只有在所有門票都售出的情況下才行得通。
questions.answer: The budget is a house of cards because it depends on every ticket being sold.
questions.answerZh: 這份預算十分脆弱，因為它建基於所有門票都能售出。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: The whole event will fail if any one of the five volunteers is absent.
questions.promptZh: 五名義工之中只要有一人缺席，整個活動便會失敗。
questions.answer: The event plan is a house of cards because it needs all five volunteers.
questions.answerZh: 這個活動計劃十分脆弱，因為五名義工缺一不可。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: Her argument depends entirely on one fact that nobody has checked.
questions.promptZh: 她的論點完全依賴一項沒有人核實過的事實。
questions.answer: Her argument is a house of cards because it depends on one fact that nobody has checked.
questions.answerZh: 她的論點基礎十分脆弱，因為它完全依賴一項未經核實的事實。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: The timetable works only when every train arrives exactly on time.
questions.promptZh: 這份時間表只有在每班列車都準時抵達時才行得通。
questions.answer: The timetable is a house of cards because every train must arrive on time.
questions.answerZh: 這份時間表十分脆弱，因為每班列車都必須準時抵達。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: One student is doing almost all the work. If she leaves, the group project will stop.
questions.promptZh: 一名學生幾乎負責所有工作。假如她退出，小組專題便會停下來。
questions.answer: The group project is a house of cards because one student is doing almost all the work.
questions.answerZh: 這個小組專題十分脆弱，因為幾乎所有工作都由一名學生負責。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: The savings plan works only if there are no unexpected costs.
questions.promptZh: 這個儲蓄計劃只有在沒有突如其來的開支時才行得通。
questions.answer: The savings plan is a house of cards because it works only when there are no unexpected costs.
questions.answerZh: 這個儲蓄計劃十分脆弱，因為它只有在沒有突如其來的開支時才行得通。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: The restaurant can remain open only if one large weekend event takes place.
questions.promptZh: 這間餐廳只有在一項大型週末活動如期舉行時才能繼續營業。
questions.answer: The restaurant’s plan is a house of cards because it depends on one weekend event.
questions.answerZh: 這間餐廳的計劃十分脆弱，因為它依賴一項週末活動。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: The project had no spare money, no extra time and no second plan. It was weak from the beginning.
questions.promptZh: 這個項目沒有備用資金、額外時間或第二個方案，一開始便十分脆弱。
questions.answer: The project was a house of cards from the beginning.
questions.answerZh: 這個項目從一開始便像紙牌屋一樣脆弱。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: The team was once stable, but several workers have left and no one has replaced them.
questions.promptZh: 這個團隊以往運作穩定，但幾名員工已離職，而且沒有人接替他們。
questions.answer: The team has become a house of cards since several workers left.
questions.answerZh: 幾名員工離職後，這個團隊已變得十分脆弱。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: The plan may look safe, but it depends on receiving one payment next week.
questions.promptZh: 這個計劃可能看來穩妥，但它依賴下星期收到的一筆款項。
questions.answer: The plan may be a house of cards because it depends on one payment.
questions.answerZh: 這個計劃可能十分脆弱，因為它依賴一筆款項。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: If the main player leaves, the whole team may fail very quickly.
questions.promptZh: 假如主力球員離隊，整支球隊可能會很快失去運作能力。
questions.answer: The team could collapse like a house of cards if the main player leaves.
questions.answerZh: 假如主力球員離隊，整支球隊可能會像紙牌屋一樣迅速崩潰。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: Unless the organisers add another source of power, one broken cable could stop the whole show.
questions.promptZh: 除非主辦人增加另一個電力來源，否則一條電線損壞便可能令整場表演停頓。
questions.answer: The show will be a house of cards unless the organisers add another source of power.
questions.answerZh: 除非主辦人增加另一個電力來源，否則整場表演的安排會十分脆弱。
questions.targetMeaning: A plan, system, organisation, argument or situation that appears complete or successful but is actually very weak and could easily fail if one part goes wrong.

questions.prompt: Everyone thought the plan was strong, but one small delay caused every later step to fail.
